paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: Now take a moment to dedicate the good seeds of this meditation. Dedicate them to being a path for you to have deep realizations into reality. Dedicate them to your future you — the one who's going to be incredibly capable of serving other people. Take three long exhales. And when you're ready, you can open your eyes.

chapters.title: Sharing — Childhood Memories and Their Seeds

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So — what cool things did you remember from your childhood? And what seeds did you think created them? Raise your hand. Come on, don't be shy.

paragraphs.speaker: Audience
paragraphs.text: When I was young, I used to really enjoy watching all the music-related programs on TV — MTV, or Billboard. Every week at a certain time, I would stick myself in front of the TV to hear that music and watch those programs. I really, really enjoyed it. Maybe in the past I used to be a DJ or a VJ — so that's why I get that kind of experience. And maybe a reason I feel so close to Geshe Michael is that I also enjoy a lot of rock and roll music.

paragraphs.speaker: Audience
paragraphs.text: When I was little, I had a little blanket that I really liked to rub. I would rub it until it was all worn out — in the end it all became like threads, like a little towel — and I'm still looking for a substitute, but I can't find one. I really enjoyed it. I think it feels like hugging a baby — that comfort. So I feel like maybe it came from having given people hugs in the past and making them feel comfortable that way. And maybe because I nurse my baby, maybe it also comes from that. My son is actually now holding onto the blanket I had when I was in college. I found the substitute, and now he's using it.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: So your son has this inheritance too.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: I've been doing this meditation for a while, and all of a sudden these weird memories just keep popping up. The one that came up in this meditation was: I really liked my mom's mac and cheese. She made this incredibly creamy cheese sauce that just melts in your mouth. All these cool things start arising — things I haven't thought about for years and years and years. So I invite you, after this week — and Angel, I invite you, in the review groups, to choose one of these meditations and do it for a week at a time. At first you might feel you can't remember much, but slowly these memories come flooding out. Like: why did I love this macaroni and cheese, which is a very, very American meal? At the taste of it, I almost want to go visit my mom and say, "can you make this?" — even though I don't really eat gluten or cheese anymore. But I'll make an exception, Mom — just make me my mac and cheese. Because it's also generating a feeling, right? A feeling that maybe you forgot was possible. And reconnecting with those things — and then thinking about: what does this have to do with seeing emptiness directly? Have a good think about it.

paragraphs.speaker: Timothy Lowenhaupt
paragraphs.text: All right, class is over. Thank you for meditating. We'll be back in 30 minutes for a class with Dr. Mendoza. He's going to finish up the class on what causes a rebirth as an animal, and then a class on the specifics of the kinds of sufferings of being a human. So you don't want to miss it. Take a half-hour break, and we'll see you shortly. Thank you.
